Parent: Yes... his fingers are shorter than usual. We were told it's just something he was born with and doesn't affect anything else.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has difficulty swallowing certain textures and often gags on her food, requiring work with her to make mealtime less stressful.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient: The patient has palatal abnormalities that specialists are monitoring, leading to concern about her future.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have palatal abnormalities, potentially affecting speech and feeding.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has palatal abnormalities that specialists are monitoring, leading to concern about her future.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have palatal abnormalities, potentially affecting speech and feeding.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have dental concerns, including tooth sensitivity and possible enamel weakness.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient requires extra help in school, with some going to a mainstream primary school but needing additional support in secondary school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have learning difficulties, with some needing extra help in school and others benefiting from specialized education.

a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits behavioral differences, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and anxiety.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome exhibit behavioral differences, including ASD, ADHD, and anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of her spinal bones, causing an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and short fingers with a curvature of the 5th finger (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have skeletal abnormalities, including an unusual structure of the spinal bones and short fingers.

a) Screening for heart valve issues: Regular check-ups to monitor the valve issue.
b) Monitoring palatal abnormalities: Keeping an eye on the palatal abnormalities.
c) Managing feeding difficulties: Working with the patient to make mealtime less stressful.
d) Addressing tooth sensitivity: Avoiding cold foods and seeking treatment for tooth sensitivity.
e) Monitoring growth: Checking the patient's growth velocity and considering referrals for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.
Parent: Oh, yes... my baby squints quite a bit, and it's really concerning because I worry it might affect his ability to learn and interact with others. I've tried to get him to wear glasses, but he doesn't like them very much.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: Well... he does get frustrated when there's too much noise around him. Like in malls or at school. It's almost as if the sounds overwhelm him. But otherwise, his hearing seems fine.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: Poor thing... his teeth break or chip so easily! It's like they're made of glass or something. We have to be super careful what he eats and make sure he brushes them just right.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: Yes... he gets tired more quickly than the other kids. Even after just playing for a little while. It worries me because I want him to be able to run around and have fun like everyone else.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: He has hypotonia... low muscle tone. The physiotherapist says it's why he has trouble with certain movements and balance. We're working on exercises to help strengthen his muscles.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach, bowel).
Parent: Actually... yes. He has a feeding aversion. Certain foods just don't agree with him. And sometimes... well... let's just say mealtime can be challenging.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: There are these undescended testes... and how he moves is a bit different from his friends. Not in a bad way... just... unique. And the doctor did mention something about needing to monitor those testes further.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a slightly different heart structure compared to the normal population, and the specialist mentioned it during the initial consultation.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient shows selective eating habits, refusing food and becoming stressed during mealtime, leading to potential nutritional deficiencies and health complications.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome exhibit feeding difficulties, requiring short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits clumsiness and poor coordination, suggesting possible brain-related issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and around 38% have heart conditions.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences difficulty focusing on objects and rubbing her eyes, indicating potential visual and ocular issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome exhibit feeding difficulties, requiring short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has vision problems such as astigmatism, short-sightedness, and squinting, potentially affecting reading and social interactions.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's teeth are weak, and taking proper care of them is important.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient's cognitive abilities and learning difficulties may impact academic performance, requiring additional support in school.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and around 38% have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient displays clumsiness and poor coordination, suggesting possible brain-related issues.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and around 38% have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, giving rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and some have short fingers with a curvature of the 5th finger (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Screen for hearing and vision issues early in life.
b) Regularly screen for heart conditions, especially in infants and young children.
c) Refer for orthodontic evaluation if weak teeth are noted.
d) Consider a palate review if feeding difficulties or speech concerns are present.
e) Perform regular dental check-ups.
f) Conduct hearing evaluations starting at age 5.
g) Review the positioning of testes in boys.
h) Evaluate the presence of tethered cord and perform MRI if clinically indicated.
i) Monitor growth velocity and refer for endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
j) Implement physical therapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, and behavioral therapy based on the patient's needs.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a valve abnormality in his heart, requiring regular monitoring to ensure it does not impact his daily life or activity levels.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences constipation, which is an ongoing issue that requires dietary changes and occasional medication to manage.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures, and around 38% have heart conditions.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences seizures, which are being managed with medication and worked closely with his neurologist to adjust treatments as needed.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has palatal abnormalities that were identified during a previous examination and are under observation, with follow-up appointments to assess any developments or necessary interventions.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have palatal abnormalities.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences vision problems such as astigmatism and short-sightedness (myopia and hypermetropia), and squint (strabismus), which can affect speech development and feeding.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have vision problems.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences tooth sensitivity, particularly when eating cold foods, which has made meal times challenging.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have tooth sensitivity.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school, and some may need to transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Educational Health Care Plans (EHCP).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have seizures.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, and anxiety, and may require medication.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 20-40% of people with KBG syndrome have behavioral differences.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has an unusual structure of their spinal bones, giving rise to an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis), and short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the 5th fingers (clinodactyly).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Screening for vision and hearing: Regular assessments for vision and hearing are recommended to monitor progress and address any issues.
b) Monitoring of heart condition: Regular monitoring of the heart condition is essential to ensure it does not impact the patient's daily life or activity levels.
c) Management of seizures: The patient is being managed with medication and works closely with his neurologist to adjust treatments as needed.
d) Management of digestive issues: Dietary changes and occasional medication help manage constipation, but it remains a challenge that requires ongoing attention.
e) Management of palatal abnormalities: Follow-up appointments are scheduled to assess any developments or necessary interventions for palatal abnormalities.

a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has a valvular abnormality or similar issue affecting her heart valve, requiring frequent check-ups.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient struggles with mealtime, becoming picky about food and having difficulty eating.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many babies with KBG syndrome have feeding difficulties, and some require short-term nasogastric tube feeding to supplement oral feeds.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has hypotonia, with stiff muscles that affect her movement and balance, making it hard to see her struggle.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Hypotonia is a common feature in KBG syndrome, characterized by weakened muscle tone.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient experiences palatal abnormalities, suggesting potential issues with speech and feeding.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Palatal abnormalities are a known feature of KBG syndrome, potentially impacting speech and feeding.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has palatal abnormalities, indicating potential issues with speech and feeding.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Palatal abnormalities are a known feature of KBG syndrome, potentially impacting speech and feeding.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient: N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: N/A

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has weak enamel and requires careful toothbrushing to prevent cavities.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Many people with KBG syndrome have weak enamel, increasing the risk of cavities.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient: The patient needs extra help in school, particularly with speech delays and behavioral differences.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Children with KBG syndrome typically require additional support in school, especially with speech delays and behavioral differences.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient: The patient exhibits behavioral differences, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and anxiety.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Behavioral differences are common in KBG syndrome, including ASD, ADHD, and anxiety.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient: The patient has brachydactyly (short fingers) with a possible clinodactyly (curved 5th finger), and may have an increased curvature of the spine (scoliosis).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome: Skeletal abnormalities, such as brachydactyly and scoliosis, are common in KBG syndrome.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Screen for heart valve abnormalities and perform echocardiograms and electrocardiograms (ECGs) as recommended.
b) Perform regular hearing assessments starting at age 5, and refer for ophthalmological evaluations as needed.
c) Conduct regular dental check-ups and ensure proper tooth brushing techniques.
d) Refer for orthopedic evaluation if asymmetrical hip creases or painful gait are noted.
e) Consider a palate review if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns.
f) Schedule periodic cardiac check-ups, including echocardiograms and ECGs, as recommended.
g) Monitor growth velocity and consider endocrine investigations if height is below the 2nd centile.
